So I'm doing an idea I had a while ago.

Each game will be 2 heroes and a support deck at (H)=3.  Each match is based around a nemesis pairing, the main Hero gets to bring a friend, and then I pick a support deck that isn't overpowered and has thematically solid character cards.  (the support deck is 5 Hero Character cards on their incap side, they count as the third hero, on the support deck turn each hero picks an incap from the top card, then discard it, when the deck is empty it gets reshuffled)  I'll do one for each environment.

I imagine these events to be part of an "Alternate Destiny" line of one-shots that don't affect canon.

I'll log them all here if anyone wants to look and see how they go.

#1.  The Block:  Vengeful Baron Blade (adv) vs. Legacy and Bunker (AZ, F6tempest, Tachyon, AZ, Waith)

The freedom 5 assembles, Baron Blade has gotten loose in the Block and they need help containing him.  Little do they know they are walking into a trap.  The rest of the team is seperated from them as Baron Blade springs his trap, and his chance at vengence is at hand.

Result:  Blade wins. Probably shouldn't have played him on advanced.

#2.  The Final Wasteland:  Akash'Bhuta vs. The Argent Adept and Ra (Fanatic, EHaka, Tempest, The Scholar, Visionary)

The Argent Adept woke up, and looked around him.  "Quiet my friend, it hunts us still."  Blake was gone from the face of his ally, the being before him burned with the power of a god.  "We have to face it, it's the only way to end this."  Anthony replied, "I am ready."  Ra thought of the friends they had lost since falling through the portal into this cursed land.

"Then let us face this destiny together."

Result:  Easy win for heroes, Akash at (H)=3 is weak, esp. non-advanced.

#3.  Insula Primalis:  Ambuscade (adv) vs. Haka and Bunker EOW (Tachyon, TempestF6, Fanatic, Ra, Adept)

Haka stepped off the plane with Stephen Graves.

"Thank you for helping me, we cannot allow the hunter to kill these animals, they are the last of their kind."  Haka said to the one man who could stand toe to toe with him.

"It's the least I can do, I must atone for the wrongs of my life."

Result:  Ambuscade wins.  3 quick Obsidian fields made it a quick match a last turn chain of cards for Ambuscade won him the match, he was dead if we lived.

#4.  Megalopolis:  Omnitron (adv) vs. Omnitron-X and Unity (Expat, RCWraith, Legacy, Visionary, Tempest {no play a card abilities})

"Where are you taking me?"  Unity asked the robot from the future.

"You must follow.  You must help." was the reply she got.

He led her to the Entrance of a large warehouse that had all sorts of warning signs on it.  When the doors opened she could see why they were there.

"I thought it was destroyed. . ."

"Intruders must not survive." The massive machine rose up, the building folding and twisting into the sides of the robot.

Result:  Omnitron wins.  No equipment for Unity and 2 EPE's early on for Omni made it a quick game.  Crappy game all around.

#5.  Pike Industrial Complex:  Friend of My BiL was over, we played a game in Pike vs. the rat, didn't follow the nemesis mode, but we won.  Fanatic Legacy Visionary and Adv. Rat had Fanatic at +4 before TtE, she did 40 damage to Rat round two. (16 self damage)

#6.  Realm of discord:  People still over, did Gloomy (adv) in Realm of Discord with Nightmist, Fixer and RC Wraith, win by knocking out Gloomy's health, Nightmist redirecting portal fiend while Wraith fed the environment trash.

#7.  Rook City:  Tried my Spite remake, really liked it, was a nasty match, but quick.

posts.name: Mezike
posts.cooked:
I wouldn't say that the combos were strange, they were just things that I had never done before or had the need to consider. For example, whilst Fixer was caught in the brambles I was making heavy use of Toolbox - I've always considered him a very versatile character but had never truly seen that in action until I spammed Toolbox for a couple of turns. He turned into a real powerhouse whilst allowing the other characters to keep their weapons in action.

The most fun moment was when Bunker dropped into turret mode then ran out of cards to power the gatling gun. I figured I would let it go and make a tough choice between continuing to heap on the damage as we were suffering from the -1 to Villain targets, or to drop out of turret mode to recharge cards with no guarantee of getting back there again. Wraith peeked into the villain deck and we were going to be hit with losing either Ongoings or Equipment, either of which would have been disasterous. Then a lightbulb went off and for the first time ever I made good use of Salvage Yard. Akash trashed Bunkers gat which was going to go anyway, Wraith trashed her stuff to make up the balance. Fixer put a heap of cards into Bunkers hand solving two problems for him at once, and also put some useful weapons back into Fixers hands at just the point that he was able to start doing some really effective damage again. I calculated that I could put Wraith into the brambles to free up Fixer and between Fixer and Bunker they would be able to wipe all of the Villain targets in one round so it made sense for the Wraith to indulge in a little self sacrifice.

It was a seamless and beautiful moment for the heroes.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Three victories today, two of them without casualties, although only one was easy.  All solo games, even though I was at a friend's house...two were before anyone else showed up (the friend in question was still doing housework and snack runs and such), and one was later while everyone else was tied up playing Stone Age.  Along with the forum game that wrapped up this morning, that means I've played in four environments today, and I have 2 days left in which to try and cover the other 8 (possibly I'll start a second loop but there's no hope of me finishing it).

Today was the first time I defeated Iron Legacy, and the first time I played against The Chairman on Advanced.  Both of those games were major workouts, while beating Plague Rat up proved to be just as much of a cakewalk with 5 heroes as with 4 (scaling the value of H on "destroy an InfectioN" damage doesn't do much, since the heroes can just stay infected and not worry about it).  I should have played on Advanced, but very likely if I had, the bonus to infected heroes' damage would have just made the game even shorter.  I have yet to lose even one hero to PR, despite him supposedly being ultra-violent, and I've never seen him flip.  Next time, definitely going for three heroes on Advanced; if that doesn't do the trick I don't know what will.

The Chairman game was simply incredible.  Being Advanced isn't entirely an advantage for him; he flips and becomes vulnerable to damage much sooner, and the huge bonus to Thugs' damage only came up once, when Bunker ran out of cards to pay the Enforcers.  Bunker died that game, but it wasn't all bad - Chrono-Ranger drew By Any Means, and you could just imagine him turning to Bunker's player and saying "Give me a card play!  Give me a card play NOW!"  Legacy started off pretty useless, apart from Galvanize, but by the end he was a ridiculous melee-immune powerhouse with about 8 ongoings in play (plus the Legacy Ring); Chrono-Ranger put three bounties on The Operative (all of which remained in play after she was incapped, since she didn't "leave play"), and quickly tore her to pieces with his compounded bow dealing 8 damage a turn.  Unfortunately he got greedy and played Hunter & Hunted to add 6 more to that, finishing her off the same turn, and then having a +3 to damage against him when the Chairman went...since he was clearly doomed anyway, he nova'ed out and beat the Chairman up some more before dying, and then came the absolute most priceless play of the game.

Undivided Attention had Mr. Pike dealing, with the bonuses from the dead Operative and two Villainous Weaponries, a total of 6 damage to the highest-HP hero, who was Nightmist - and she had The Amulet (along with the other amulet, but whenever someone says The Amulet in reference to her, they don't mean that one).  So Chairman Pike, instead of dealing 6 damage to her, dealt 6 damage to himself - and then retaliated against himself for 7!!!  Even after that hilarity, the game could still have ended in disaster if he'd ever gotten a Prison Break, but between Mistbound and Take Down, he'd skipped his card play three times (both copies of Mistbound - Misty was doing a LOT of discarding, even by her standards, this game), and the rest was just luck.  Also in the vein of luck was the turn-1 Meteor Storm which kept the heroes from getting torn up too bad by The Muscle and The Contract at the beginning of the game...the last environment plays included a Self-Destruct sequence which the heroes completely ignored, since they had the Chairman (of Mars, apparently) on the ropes at that point anyway.  All told, an awesome game, and if we weren't having a "blitz" this weekend, I'd probably rest on my laurels for a few days before playing again.

posts.name: Oaktree

Now THAT was a frustrating game.

6) Citizen Dawn at Megalopolis vs Young Legacy, Tachyon, and Bunker.

Heroes conceded in Round 6.

Game started with Citizens Spring and Sweat in play.  Truth (of course) is drawn and things will be a bit slower. 

Heroes spend Round 1 blasting Truth into the trash.  Though that will let Sweat cause more discards.  The Environment Deck now joins the fun by playing Papparazi.  (yay)

Citizen Tears comes into play in Round 2 and essentially allows Sweat to nuke even more cards.  The heroes manage to kill off Citizen Sweat, but also are almost totally out of cards due to getting Papparazi trashed.  The Environment Deck retaliates with Impending Casualty.

Citizen Dawn rolls out Return With the Dawn and gets Sweat back out of the trash. etc. etc. Environment Deck play Hostage Situation just for giggles.

Round 6 starts with THAT CARD.  Heroes have zero cards in play, zero cards in hand. 

Citizen Dawn has the following in play:  Citizens Tears, Sweat, Spring, and Truth.  Ongoing cards "Return With the Dawn" and "Channel the Eclipse".

With only Young Legacy able to deal damage by default the heroes are going to get nowhere fast.  Even if they skip actions to draw two Citizen Sweat will force a total discard.  And it will take 7 rounds at least for Young Legacy to kill Citizen Truth out unless Citizen Dare rolls out and does it for her.  Not a lot of damage being dished out yet, but that will escalate at some point given that two villain cards will be drawn per turn along with Truth coming back from the trash a turn later.

GAH.  I've seen 4-5 Round stomps of villains due to good hero draws, but this is the first time I've seen a hero team completely steamrollered* like this. *(Well, less steamrollered than effectively neutered and staked out to be nibbled to death over a extended run of rounds.)

(Nitpick at Oaktree:  It's Ambuscade, no "h".  'E is, 'ow you say, Francais, oui?  I know, I'm a terrible person.  Who also can't figure out how to do mini-text on this forum.)

It seems to be a good day for me bungling games...I did manage not to concede this one (which is good since I've conceded two games in the Realm of Discord already, and this is just sad given that it's my favorite environment overall), but after The Dreamer flipped, I completely forgot that I was playing on Advanced against her, and I had no hope whatsoever of being able to fix the error.  Why, you ask?  Because the error in question involved the heroes having a lot of Equipment including Smoke Bombs in play, and The Dreamer dealing 1 damage to every non-villain target (which, on Advanced, becomes 2 damage), with Imbued Vitality in play.  The Equipments were all 6-HP non-villain targets, so Dreamer dealt 1 damage to each of them, all of which was reduced by 1 and redirected to the hero with the highest HP.  The first time this happened, Dreamy had a +1 to damage from Dark Hero, so the highest-HP hero had taken a bunch of 1-damage hits, which under the proper rules would have been 2-damage hits and quite possibly changed his highest-hero status, so that some of the hits would go to other heroes.  The second instance of damage lacked the Dark Hero bonus and thus didn't happen at all, but would have if the Advanced text applied.

So, entirely by accident, I have now played a "half-Advanced" game, something which isn't strictly legal but which appears to have been done in some of the early Statistics Thread games (sadly, I can no longer enter a game that way even though earlier results of the sort are in the database).  At some point, I will have to fight Dreamy with only Side B getting advanced text (I must remember to have H = 3 in that game, as was the case here), and then after that fight her on Advanced on both sides (probably with H = 4 that time).

posts.cooked: Just played the most spectacularly absurd game of my career, which is saying something.  Twenty-two turns!  For a difficulty 2 villain, and not even on Advanced!  Nightmist had 20 cards in hand at the start of her turn, just before killing the villain on an incap turn.  And the whole reason the game went down the way it did was that she was reckless and endangered her comrades on turn 1, eventually resulting in their deaths in a Marsquake.  Incredible.

posts.cooked:
Last game of the night (and possibly the event since I have to pack and then travel tomorrow.)

11)  Grand Warlord Voss at Wagner Mars Base vs. Omnitron-X, Dark Visionary, and Tachyon.

Hero win in 22 rounds.  DV is keeping the villain deck in check by burying Forced Deployments, but the group is just not getting anywhere in killing Voss himself while they get weakened by minions and the Environment Deck.  A Forced Deployment does get into play, but the heroes trigger it on purpose and let a left intact Oxygen Leak kill the minion pile.  OX loses his components and that weakens the group and things look grim.   Tachyon burns out her cards and a couple of Lightspeed Barrages to do some damage, but is then taken out in Round 16.  OX has gotten some effective plating out and that is keeping a growing pile of components intact.  DV is at very low HP and generally not doing much more than Turmoil every turn to have some control over the villain deck. 

A Previously buried Forced Deployment comes up and OX triggers it on purpose at the start of its turn and proceeds to devastate the minion pile using a judicious pile of components* and a well-timed Defensive Blast.

A few rounds later of being pounded alone and Voss becomes fatally demoralized before DV finishes him off with a psychic blast.

*- At game end OX had roughly 12 cards in play including 7 components.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
I'm far too lazy and lack the concentration necessary to like solo games anywhere near as much as I like games with people.

I know it's be good for me to force myself to solo a bit, to help me learn the decks better and such, but it feels like work to a person with a condition that affects her cognitive ability a lot of the time. Solo games would be much better if I had my own personal Ronway to keep track of everything for me and correct me when I get things wrong and remind me of stuff that I've forgotten and kill off my heroes.

Oh wait, I'd prefer it didn't do that last one...
